settings.title: Settings
settings.themeHint: Pick a theme for the whole app; use the arrow keys to go from one to the next and it applies right away.
settings.terminalHelp: The font size applies to all open terminals. Zooming with Ctrl + wheel (or Ctrl +/-) in a terminal affects only that terminal, and Ctrl 0 goes back to the size set here.
settings.boldBright: Bold text in bright colors (like PuTTY)
settings.scrollOnInput: Jump to the bottom when typing
settings.scrollOnOutput: Jump to the bottom on new output
settings.behaviorHelp: With Alt, the wheel scrolls 5 times faster. Double-click selects a whole word: it stops at the characters in the list.
settings.sessionLog: Save what each terminal shows to a file
settings.connectionHelp: Keepalive and terminal type apply to new connections. Logs are saved without colors, one file per terminal, from when it opens.
settings.onConflict: If the file already exists at the destination
settings.filesHelp: With "Ask where to download" off, downloads go straight to that folder. What already exists at the destination is handled the same way in uploads, downloads and drags.
settings.verboseHelp: Verbose logging adds every connection attempt, every forward request and the like to the log, to help track down a problem. The log is in
settings.restoreSession: Restore the session when osat starts
settings.restoreHelp: When osat starts, the tabs, tiled panes and their proportions from last time come back.
settings.lockEnable: Ask for a password to open osat
settings.lockIdle: Lock after this many minutes of inactivity (0 = never)
settings.lockHelp: This is a lock screen: connections, transfers and forwards keep running behind it, and credentials stay in the system store, not encrypted again. If you forget the password, osat won't open.
settings.lockSetMsg: osat will ask for this password when it opens and when it locks.
settings.lockOffMsg: Enter the current password to turn the lock off.
settings.autoUpdate: Check for updates when osat opens
settings.autoUpdateHelp: When there's a new version, osat shows you what's in it and offers to install it: it downloads it, closes and opens again updated. Open connections close when it restarts. It checks the versions published on GitHub and doesn't send any of your data.
settings.webBrowserHelp: Shows the Sites section in the sidebar and opens web pages in a tab, keeping your login between restarts. Turning it off closes the open sites.
settings.restoreDefaultsMsg: All settings go back to their original values.
settings.defaultsHelp: Used by connections with “Use default credentials” and, when missing, by those without their own username or password. Changing the password here changes it for all of them. The password is kept in the system credential store.

form.importTip: Bring in connections from PuTTY, WinSCP, mRemoteNG or OpenSSH
form.gatewayHelp: Gateway server, as in a Windows .rdp file. Uses the same user, domain and password as the computer.
form.name: Name
form.saveSecret: Save in the system's secure store
form.agentHelp: Uses Pageant or the Windows OpenSSH agent (or ssh-agent on Linux/macOS).
form.jumpHelp: For servers that can only be reached from an SSH bastion (OpenSSH ProxyJump).
form.jumpHelpVnc: To reach a VNC server that isn't exposed: pick the SSH connection to go through. To use the server's own SSH, pick its SSH connection and enter localhost as the host.
form.jumpGatewayHelp: Can't be combined with an RD Gateway.
form.forwardAgentWarn: While the session is open, the server's administrator (root) can use your agent to authenticate elsewhere on your behalf. Enable it only on servers you trust.
form.initialCommandHelp: It is typed into the shell when each terminal of this connection opens. A single line.
form.envHelp: One per line, as NAME=value. They are sent to the server when the terminal opens, but sshd only accepts LANG and LC_* unless AcceptEnv is set in sshd_config.
form.useDefaultsHelp: Connects with the default username ({user}) and its password, from Settings → Default credentials.
form.useDefaultsNone: There are no default credentials yet: set them in Settings → Default credentials.

bridge.tokenMsg: The command you already added to Claude Code stops working: you have to add it again with the new one.
bridge.intro: With the bridge on, Claude Code (the one on this PC) can see, read and write in the terminals you share, to help you from its own terminal. Nothing needs to be installed on the servers.
bridge.portBusy: The usual port ({preferred}) was busy, so this time {port} is used. If you already added the bridge to Claude Code with port {preferred}, it won't connect until you restart osat with that port free; or add it again with the command below.
bridge.addIt: Add it to Claude Code with this command (only once):
bridge.afterwards: Then, in each terminal you want to show it, click the Claude button on its tab. While it is shared, that button stays highlighted. The other terminals are not visible.
bridge.modeAskRest: (recommended): read-only commands run without asking; everything else asks for your permission.
bridge.modeAutoRest: : Claude runs whatever it wants in the terminals you share, without asking you.
bridge.autoWarn: In this mode Claude can type and run anything in the shared terminals without your approval: on a production server or in a terminal on this PC (with your files and your keys) it can delete or change anything. Share only what you want to give it.
bridge.permsAuto: Permissions for this mode: Claude Code can use all the tools without asking.
bridge.permsAsk: Recommended permissions: read-only commands run without asking; everything else asks for your permission.
bridge.pasteC: of a project); if you already have a "permissions" section, add these lines to its "allow" (and "ask") and remove the ones from the previous mode.
bridge.pasteBold: Claude Code is the one that asks, not osat
bridge.pasteD: : changing the mode here doesn't change what Claude Code already has in its settings.json, so after changing it you have to paste these rules.
bridge.askNote: Osat only accepts as "read-only" commands it can verify (ls, cat, grep, ps, df, docker ps, git --no-pager log...) and rejects anything that chains commands, redirects, uses sudo or touches keys and passwords. Everything else goes through run_command: Claude Code asks you for permission and requires it to explain what the command does and why.
bridge.autoNote: In this mode it is also not required to explain each command.
bridge.offNote: It only listens on this PC and requires a token. Turning it off stops sharing everything.

GATEWAY.default: The connection through the gateway {gateway} failed.
GATEWAY.dns: The gateway name {gateway} wasn't found. Check that it's spelled right; if it's an internal name, it's only found with the VPN connected.

unreachable.default: Couldn't open a connection to the gateway {gateway}. Check that the VPN is connected and that the network reaches the gateway.
unreachable.timeout: The gateway {gateway} isn't responding: the connection couldn't be opened. Check that the VPN is connected and that no firewall blocks the port.
unreachable.refused: The gateway {gateway} refused the connection: there's no service on that port. Check the gateway port.

tls.default: The connection to the gateway {gateway} opened, but the secure connection (TLS) failed.
tls.rejected: The gateway {gateway} rejected the secure connection (TLS): it doesn't accept the version or ciphers osat offers.
tls.closed: The connection to the gateway {gateway} was cut when starting the secure connection (TLS). This is usually a proxy, firewall or antivirus that inspects HTTPS.
tls.timeout: The gateway {gateway} didn't complete the secure connection (TLS) in time.

GATEWAY.http: The gateway {gateway} answered HTTP {status}, which isn't the answer of an RD Gateway. Check the gateway address.
GATEWAY.noNtlm: The gateway {gateway} doesn't accept NTLM authentication, and osat doesn't support Kerberos.

notAuthorized.default: The gateway {gateway} didn't authorize the sign-in ({code}).
notAuthorized.cap: The gateway {gateway} doesn't authorize your user (connection authorization policy, CAP): it isn't in the allowed groups or the second factor was rejected.
notAuthorized.dropped: The gateway {gateway} closed the connection while authorizing the sign-in: this usually happens when the second factor is rejected or not approved.

GATEWAY.timeout: The sign-in to the gateway {gateway} wasn't approved in time. If you get a notification on your phone, approve it and reconnect.
GATEWAY.resourceDenied: The gateway {gateway} doesn't let you connect to {target} (resource authorization policy, RAP). The computer isn't among the allowed ones, or another name has to be used (the full or the short one).

targetUnreachable.connect: The gateway {gateway} couldn't connect to {target}: the computer is off, its name isn't found from the gateway or the port is blocked.
targetUnreachable.timeout: The gateway {gateway} didn't answer whether it reached {target}: the computer may be off or the port blocked from the gateway.

connectionLost.default: The connection to the gateway {gateway} was lost. Try again; if it keeps happening, the network is unstable.
connectionLost.noAnswer: The gateway {gateway} closed the connection without answering the first request (the secure connection did work). There may be a proxy or firewall in between, or the address isn't an RD Gateway.
connectionLost.channel: The gateway {gateway} closed the connection when asked to reach {target}.

RDP_SERVER.x224: The computer {host} didn't answer like a remote desktop server: the port doesn't speak RDP or the connection was cut.
RDP_SERVER.tls: Couldn't establish the secure connection (TLS) with the computer {host}.
